title: Binary computation by a finite machine
statement: Let $c$ be a program in the partial-recursive language and $f$ a function from Boolean strings to Boolean strings. Suppose that for every Boolean string $x$, evaluating $c$ on the singleton list containing the sentinel numeric code of $x$ returns the singleton list containing the sentinel numeric code of $f(x)$. Then there exist a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet and a function $T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that on every input $x$ the machine halts with output $f(x)$ after exactly $T(|x|)$ steps.

replaced:
Let $c$ be a program in Mathlib's partial-recursive language and $f$ a function on
Boolean strings such that evaluating $c$ on the singleton list holding the sentinel
numeric code of each string $x$ yields exactly the singleton list holding the code
of $f(x)$.  Then there exist a finite Turing machine over the two-letter Boolean
alphabet and a time bound $T \colon \bbn \to \bbn$ such that the machine computes
$f$, halting within $T(\abs{x})$ steps on every input $x$.
